While the load was held in position the M/V began to reverse toward the platform and under the load. . At that time, the bottom of the tote tank encountered one of the handrails of a gangway. . Customer-specific facilities charges on Sheet 17: Bellagio/Park MGM $24,728, Mandalay Bay/Excalibur/Luxor $36,770, Paris/Horseshoe $16,876 a month., Demand: the first 300 kW or less of firm billing demand 8,223.00 USD, all additional kW 21.08 USD/kW (less 0.70 USD/kW when the customer takes delivery at 69 kV or more and provides the transformation), excess on-peak demand 13.00 USD/kW more, and a coincident peak demand charge of 7.00 USD/kW. Energy: 0.0497 USD/kWh summer and winter on-peak, 0.0375 USD/kWh off-peak (plus an off-peak energy premium of 0.02287 USD/kWh for energy under the off-peak demand provision), with the fuel adjustment clause (FAC-25, Fb/Sb 0.03641 USD/kWh) and deferred cost recovery (DCR-25); no single energy charge is printed. The minimum firm billing demand factor is 100% for months 1 to 60, 95% for 61 to 120 and 90% after; the minimum coincident peak demand billing factor 50%, 65% and 80%. Before the service agreement the customer pays in full for delivery point and transmission costs (interconnection, network upgrades, redundant facilities). Experimental: available through no later than April 24, 2029; customers with loads of 100 MW or more are excluded from the 12% class size limit., Distribution is a Customer Charge only ($999.11 per month); transmission is billed under the TSC rate schedule on the customer's peak load contribution to the PJM peak load, and generation under GSC-2, so no demand or energy charge is printed on LP-6. Applies to large load (data center) customers that commenced service on or after October 1, 2025, with a peak of 50 MW or greater at a single facility or at least 75 MW in the aggregate within a 10-mile radius at or above 69 kV; a 50 to 75 MW facility that causes no transmission network upgrade costs may be petitioned into Rate LP-5. Voluntary interruptible option: the minimum load guarantee falls to 60% for the first five years and 30% for the second five (page 111)., Effective for service on 8 July 2026 (Order No. 26-239, p. 5, approving Advice No. 26-24). Order No. 26-154 (p. 45) adds a system capacity allocation deposit due at contract signing equal to two years of minimum transmission demand, refundable at 50 percent in year two and 50 percent in year three after energization if the customer meets 80 percent of its allocated system capacity and its contracted flexibility plan., Energy is charged in three blocks: First 500,000 kWh 5.745 cents per kWh, Next 5,500,000 kWh 5.160 cents per kWh, All Over 6,000,000 kWh 4.211 cents per kWh (page 1); energy_charge is the last block, the one a load of more than 6,000,000 kWh a month pays at the margin. Demand: $47,891.00 for the first 3,000 kVa of demand or less, and $12.98 per kVa for each additional kVa of demand (page 1). Primary voltage discounts of $0.20, $1.52 and $4.39 per kVa of demand per month at 11 kV, 60 kV and 115 kV or higher (page 1). Annual minimum $1,177,388 (Schedule 25A, page 2). The monthly rate is subject to Schedules 58, 61, 63, 66, 88, 91, 92, 93, 98 and 99 (page 2)., Proposed: a settlement filed 6 October 2026, pending NCUC approval as of 12 November 2026. Applies to letter agreements and electric service agreements executed on and after 1 June 2026. Contract term: below 100 MW the greater of 10 years and 5 years plus the load ramp period; 100 MW or more the greater of 15 years and 10 years plus the load ramp period., Proposed: filed 2 April 2026 with a requested effective date of 3 May 2026 (the date written), suspended 120 days by Decision No. C26-0280 of 30 April 2026; final decision not read. The 15-year minimum initial term is now read in primary documents (session 3937, window P4's research pass, 13 November 2026, row xcel_plains-03): PSCo's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 ('The proposed tariff also includes a minimum initial term of 15 years, minimum bill provisions, termination and exit fees, and credit requirements'; 'A CPUC decision is expected in late 2026 or early 2027') and the Colorado PUC's Electric Rate Cases page ('Requiring large customers to sign contracts of 15 years or more'; 'New customers using between 20 and 50 MW may also be subject to the tariff'; the Commission's decision 'TBD'). Leads from intervenor testimony, still not verified in the filing: minimum monthly bill on 80 percent of contract capacity; an optional ramp of up to 5 years within the term; exit fee the sum of the remaining minimum monthly bills., Proposed: the companies ask an expedited ruling on the form (p. 7); the statutory period runs to 2 December 2026 (p. 6). Termination by the customer after long-term supply begins, on not less than 36 months' notice (p. 149). The June 2026 fact sheet (https://www.nvenergy.com/publish/content/dam/nvenergy/brochures_arch/help/brochures/Large-Load-Electric-Service-Agreement-LLESA-Fact-Sheet.pdf, read 2026-11-12) says the LLESA serves customers whose energy needs typically exceed 25 MW., Schedule 94 (https://www.grantpud.org/templates/galaxy/images/images/Downloads/Rates/NewLargeLoadService94/Sch_94_Jan_1_2016_-_Final.pdf): a New Large Load's monthly energy charge is the greater of the month's weighted average ICE Mid-C index price (peak and off-peak) or the largest energy block on Schedule 15, plus a 5% premium; its demand charges are those of the underlying schedule. Schedule 15's own energy charges (PRP 0.02548, incremental 0.00260 and temporary stabilization 0.00520 USD per kWh) apply to loads that are not New Large Loads. Billing demand is the larger of the contract demand or the month's highest 15-minute demand adjusted up to a 95 percent power factor. Customer Service Policy section 2.3: "Service to New Large Loads will only be made pursuant to Rate Schedule No. 94"; section 8 sets the large power application, inquiry form and fees., The Commission's modification lets the customer's financial sponsor meet the collateral as a co-signer (p. 150). Ramp floors of 50, 65, 80 and 90 percent of contract capacity in years 1 to 4 (p. 91). The 1st Revised sheets effective 28 August 2026 (Case 26-113-EL-ATA) are held for a license and not written., The charges are NOVEC's distribution charges (Part B); energy supply (Part A) is bought from NOVEC under the Market Based Rate Option, "to be determined on a case by case basis", so no supply price is printed. Billing demand is the higher of the month's highest 30-minute kW or the contract minimum times the contract's ramp-up percentages; billing energy the higher of metered kWh or billing demand times the month's hours times 0.85. An rKVA charge of $0.16 per rKVA is printed beside the demand charge, and monthly fixed charge rates on contributed capital for excess facilities (0.442% high voltage line, 0.644% substation, 0.893% primary distribution). The minimum monthly distribution charge is the amount in the contract. Not for back-up or standby service. NOVEC announced a filing to update its terms and conditions in July 2026 (news release nr071726); this schedule is the one its Regulated Rates page links on 18 November 2026., The contract provisions apply to customers taking initial service and signing an ESA on or after 1 January 2027 (p. 32); a load ramp period of up to four years within the term, with a minimum annual ramp of 20 percent (p. 32); contracted capacity may be reduced by up to 20 percent at no cost and by a further 30 percent if another customer assumes it, each on a separate 36-month notice (p. 35); PJM capacity expense excluded from the minimum generation charge (p. 34). Appeal pending (Dominion's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026)., The figures are the distribution delivery charges of section IV-A-3, open to every qualifying customer (A-1 and A-2 are closed: demand 1.68 and 2.77 USD/kW). Electricity supply is billed at the prevailing ODEC transmission level demand and energy rates adjusted for distribution losses, with an excess demand charge of 42.5% of ODEC's owned resources demand charge, so no supply price is printed. Distribution billing demand is the greater of the month's highest 15-minute kW or 500 kW. A facilities charge applies to dedicated local facilities (1.43% a month of installed cost for standard plant without a contribution, down to 0.82% with one). A customer may end its facilities contract by paying the unamortized value of the facilities plus removal.
